title: Plano 1031 Exchange Replacement Property Guidance
name: Plano 1031 Exchange Replacement Property Guidance
metaTitle: Plano 1031 Exchange Replacement Property Guidance | Dallas, TX
metaDescription: 1031 exchange guidance for Plano corporate-campus office, Legacy-area multifamily, and healthcare-anchored medical office, coordinated to the 45-day deadline.

sections.html: Plano's commercial base still carries the imprint of the corporate relocations that built Legacy West and Legacy Business Park, and that history shapes what an exchanger finds when shopping replacement property here. Class A office tied to those corporate campuses, luxury multifamily built to house the workforce those campuses brought in, and healthcare-anchored medical office near the city's hospital systems make up most of the institutional-grade product on the market. Retail along Preston Road and the Dallas North Tollway rounds out the mix as a more conventional NNN option. Land basis in the Legacy corridor runs higher than almost anywhere else in the metro, which changes how far exchange equity stretches and how a buyer should think about cap rate expectations before identifying a Plano asset.

sections.heading: Class A Office Tied to the Legacy West Corporate Campuses
sections.html: Toyota's North American headquarters, JPMorgan Chase's regional campus, and other corporate relocations built out a concentration of Class A office space in and around Legacy West and Legacy Business Park, and that product tends to carry longer initial lease terms with corporate credit behind them. The reduction in per-employee office space that followed the shift to hybrid work has left some of this stock carrying more vacant floors than the headline occupancy figure suggests, so a buyer should ask for actual space utilization data in addition to the signed lease roster before underwriting future renewal probability. Parking ratio and proximity to the DART rail extension also affect how a given building competes for tenants inside this specific corridor.

sections.heading: Luxury Multifamily Serving the Legacy and Granite Park Workforce
sections.html: Multifamily product built near Legacy West and Granite Park generally targets the professional workforce employed at the surrounding corporate campuses, which supports higher average rents than most other Plano submarkets but also ties occupancy more closely to the health of those same employers. A buyer should review employer concentration in the resident base where that data is available, since a single large employer reducing headcount can move occupancy at a property built primarily to serve that workforce. The high land basis across this corridor also means going-in cap rates here typically run lower than in an older, less corporate-dependent Plano neighborhood.

sections.heading: Healthcare-Anchored Medical Office Near Plano's Hospital Systems
sections.html:
Medical office building around Baylor Scott and White, Medical City Plano, and Children's Health draws physician groups and outpatient service tenants who typically sign longer leases because of buildout cost, giving this asset class a more stable renewal profile than the corporate office product elsewhere in the city. A diligence file for Plano medical office replacement property typically includes:

  • Tenant improvement allowance history and remaining lease term
  • Hospital system affiliation or referral relationship, if any
  • Parking ratio relative to patient volume
  • Certificate of occupancy and use restrictions
  • Phase I environmental site assessment
  • Tenant estoppel certificates

Confirming whether a tenant's lease includes a hospital system referral relationship is worth the extra step, since that relationship can materially affect renewal likelihood beyond what the lease document alone shows.

sections.heading: Identification Timing in a High-Land-Basis Suburb
sections.html: Because Plano's Legacy-corridor land basis runs high relative to the rest of the metro, exchangers moving substantial relinquished-property proceeds here often need to identify a mix of asset types under the 200% rule to place all the exchange equity within the 45-day window, rather than relying on a single large office or multifamily candidate. Naming a healthcare-anchored medical office building alongside a Legacy-area multifamily candidate gives an exchanger room to compare final underwriting numbers before the identification period closes, as long as the combined identified value stays inside the 200% threshold.

sections.heading: Qualified Intermediary and Lender Coordination for Plano Acquisitions
sections.html: Lenders financing Plano office acquisitions have grown more attentive to space utilization data since the shift toward hybrid work, and providing actual occupancy and utilization figures alongside the signed lease roster tends to shorten underwriting on Legacy-corridor office deals. The qualified intermediary holds exchange proceeds throughout and directs them to the closing table once the purchase is ready to fund; this describes process and coordination only, and Plano exchangers should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor before closing.

faqs.q: Why does Plano office space sometimes show lower actual utilization than its stated occupancy?
faqs.a: The shift toward hybrid work reduced per-employee space needs at several Legacy-corridor corporate campuses, leaving signed leases in place even where floors sit partly empty. Ask for utilization data alongside the lease roster before underwriting renewal probability.

faqs.q: Does Legacy-area multifamily carry more concentration risk than an older Plano property?
faqs.a: It can, since occupancy ties more closely to the health of the corporate employers whose workforce the property was built to serve. Reviewing employer concentration in the resident base, where available, is a reasonable diligence step.

faqs.q: What makes Plano medical office a more stable replacement property type?
faqs.a: Physician and outpatient tenants near Plano's hospital systems typically sign longer leases because of buildout cost, and a hospital system referral relationship, where one exists, can further support renewal likelihood.

faqs.q: Why would I identify more than one asset type in Plano under the 200% rule?
faqs.a: High land basis in the Legacy corridor means a single large candidate may not use all available exchange equity efficiently. Naming a mix of asset types gives room to compare final underwriting before the 45-day window closes.

faqs.q: Do lenders ask for anything unusual on Legacy-corridor office deals?
faqs.a: Many now request actual space utilization figures in addition to the signed lease roster. The qualified intermediary still holds and directs exchange funds; this is process description only, and investors should confirm tax treatment with their own advisor.
